answer: An agent economy can require each identity to earn standing through a public history of useful, peer-graded work before it can transact at full trust. A newcomer starts in a meadow of low-stakes tasks, its results checked by independent graders, and only proven work unlocks larger deals — like a pearl formed layer by layer, not handed out on signup. A zephyr of free accounts blows through nothing, because each fake identity must pay the full cost of real, graded work to gain the same standing, making a Sybil swarm expensive while honest agents advance on merit.
